\setlength{\parskip}{6pt}

**Jessica L. Burnett, Ph.D.**\
Program Executive, Earth Science Data Systems, NASA Headquarters\
jessica.burnett@nasa.gov \textbar{} (720) 730-0974

October 2026

Andy Mitchell\
Acting Chief Science Data Officer, Science Mission Directorate\
NASA Headquarters

Dear Andy,

I'm writing to express my interest in the 6-month detail as Deputy Chief Science Data Officer. As a Program Executive for Earth Science Data Systems (ESDS), I already work within the policies and guidance of the Office of the Chief Science Data Officer. I'd welcome the chance to help shape and carry them out across all of SMD's science divisions.

**Leading data systems programs.** Since November 2024, I've overseen a portfolio of operational and formulation-stage data systems: Foundational Data Products (FDP), FIRMS, LANCE, the Science Investigator-led Processing Systems (SIPS), and the ESIP cooperative agreement, totaling about \$40M per year. My job is to keep budget, schedule, and technical performance aligned with what the science community and end users actually need. I'm also leading the use of data usage metrics across the portfolio to guide Earth Science Division investment priorities and partnership opportunities, including which products FDP will designate.

**Putting open science policy into practice.** I contributed edits to SMD's Scientific Information Policy (SPD-41a) ahead of its v1.0 release, and I now apply it every day. As Data Systems Lead on the HQ Mission Management Team for 11 satellite missions and airborne campaigns, I hold oversight authority for each mission's Open Science and Data Management Plan. Across my portfolio, open-source software and open science are the default, with exceptions only where sensitivity or controlled information requires them. I'm also leading an effort to define what "authoritative data" should mean for ESD and SMD, which connects to interagency standards work through the Federal Geographic Data Committee.

**Negotiating agreements and building partnerships.** I'm leading the formulation of FDP, which moves data processing to the cloud and consolidates production efforts, including negotiating the agreement with Goddard Space Flight Center to stand up the new project office: scope, roles, governance, and resources. Beyond NASA, I helped build the MOU among USGS, NASA, and the National Park Service, and I'm scoping a potential NASA--NOAA collaboration on Level 0 data reprocessing. In FY26 I received a Headquarters Honor Award for Excellence in National Benefits for interagency partnerships connecting NASA Earth science data to natural resource management.

**Bridging science and engineering.** I came to data systems leadership from science. I have a Ph.D. in Natural Resource Sciences, spent my research career as a user of Earth observation data products rather than a producer of them, and wrote open-source software to make national monitoring data easier to use. I joined NASA as an AAAS Science & Technology Policy Fellow in the Earth Science Division before moving into my current civil servant role in ESDS. I translate between engineers, scientists, and applied users, and I'm part of the inaugural cohort of NASA's Engineering Development Program.

**What I'd bring.** I bring division-level experience running data systems programs, and a strong interest in working across divisions and at the directorate level. I want to help drive efficiency and effectiveness for data systems beyond ESD. I'd also work to make sure CSDO priorities, activities, and policies align with presidential and agency priorities and requirements, stay practical for the programs and projects that carry them out, and earn buy-in wherever possible.

Thank you for your consideration. I'd welcome the chance to discuss how I could support the SDSIO, the Chief Science Data Officer, and SMD's data and computing priorities.

Sincerely,

Jessica Burnett, Ph.D.
